**Discpress 1.2.1 fixes Dreamcast CHDs and now makes the same files as chdman 0.289.** It also stops a few kinds of disc files from getting stuck.

## Download

**[⬇ discpress.html](https://github.com/PowerBeef/discpress/releases/download/v1.2.1/discpress.html)** (about 2.7 MB). The whole app in one file that works offline. To update, download it and use it instead of your old copy.

## Please convert your Dreamcast games again

Dreamcast CHDs made with Discpress 1.0.0 to 1.2.0 have a track layout that chdman 0.289 never produced:

- **Flycast up to version 2.7 refuses to load them.**
- **Games converted from a .gdi file also have their data in the wrong place** for MAME and for newer Flycast builds.

Discpress now lays out Dreamcast discs exactly like chdman 0.289. If you made Dreamcast CHDs with an earlier version, convert them again from the original .gdi or .cue files.

Other CHDs don't need converting again: their contents have always matched chdman 0.289's.

## Exactly chdman 0.289

Earlier versions were built from a MAME development snapshot taken after the 0.289 release, not from the release itself. That snapshot compresses with a different LZMA setting and contains the Dreamcast change above. So the earlier release notes were wrong to say the CHDs were the same byte for byte as desktop chdman 0.289's. Apart from Dreamcast discs, only the checksums were the same.

Discpress 1.2.1 uses the official 0.289 release:

- **Data discs:** the CHDs are the same byte for byte as the official chdman 0.289's.
- **CD audio:** a few compressed bytes can still differ, because the FLAC encoder's floating-point math isn't identical in every build. The audio itself, and the CHD's checksums, are the same.
- **Speed:** the official release compresses a little harder than that snapshot did, so creating a CHD takes about 6% longer for a CD and 12% longer for a DVD than with 1.2.0. The files come out the same size, to within 0.1%.

## Files that used to get stuck

- **Cue sheets with a byte order mark, in UTF-16 or Windows-1252, with classic Mac OS line endings, or with lower-case keywords now convert normally.** chdman misread them: it either stopped with an error or saw no tracks and ran forever.
- **.iso files that contain raw 2,352-byte CD sectors now get the right sector type.** chdman on its own guesses the type from the file size and can get it wrong, which makes a CHD that emulators can't read.
- **TOC files with one file per track keep every track.** chdman writes this kind of TOC itself when extracting with one .bin per track, and converting one back used to lose every track after the first.
- **Cue and TOC files that chdman can't convert now say why** instead of starting a job that never ends: no tracks, a track number outside 01–99, or a track length chdman can't read.
- **A binary .toc next to a cue sheet is skipped.** Some disc dumping tools save one.
- **If chdman ever stops making progress, the job is stopped** with an explanation instead of running forever. This covers commands in the Advanced tab too.

## Also fixed

**Dreamcast CHDs made by chdman 0.289 are recognized as Dreamcast games.** Before, the app could read the disc's small first area instead of the game area and name the wrong console.
